raw_response:
I’m not going to spread myself too thin this year. On 12 mu with only two people in the household, labor is a real constraint, even if I know how to push yield. I’ll keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is my most reliable base: wheat gives me stability, and maize follows immediately with a familiar management schedule. I’ll keep 4 mu in cotton because I’ve grown it a long time and I know how to manage water and insects on it. Chili can make money, but it is labor-intensive and the disease risk is higher, so I’ll hold it to 2 mu only. With my experience, I do make adjustments by crop stage and soil condition, but I still stay close to what has worked on my own fields and what fits a two-person household.

For wheat, I’ll use a fairly standard split application: base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress at jointing if the stand and color justify it. I won’t cut nitrogen too hard because wheat responds clearly here, and I have well irrigation, so I can support the crop. For maize, the turnaround after wheat harvest is tight, so I’ll use simple field preparation and plant quickly with hybrid seed. Cotton and chili need more watching than the grain crops, especially for insects and picking labor, so I’m keeping their area controlled. I can afford to manage all four crops, but only if I stay disciplined on area and don’t chase every high-input option.
